clue.text: Church official drops last letter by the roadside

definitions.note: a noun used attributively here: the verge is the grass strip at the side of a road

indicators.note: drops last letter tells us to shed the final letter of the official's title

parts.note: a verger is a church caretaker who leads processions

explanation.surface: A clergyman's assistant loses a letter somewhere along the side of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is the grassy edge bordering a road, so it is the strip found at the roadside.

clue.text: Flow out from mean tea, stirred

indicators.note: stirred suggests the letters are mixed like tea in a cup

explanation.surface: Something seeps out of a stingy cup of tea once it's stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or spread out from a source.

clue.text: White mongrel reversing round outdoor statue

indicators.note: reversing says the hidden letters are read backwards
round says the two words wrap around the answer, which sits within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pale crossbred dog backs up around a garden ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had 'round' in the definition, leaving the hidden word unsignalled; 'round' is better read as the words going round the answer, and 'outdoor statue' alone defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden gnome is a small ornamental figure of a bearded dwarf placed outside.

parts.note: like means as, in the sense 'in the same way as'
the writer's tool is a pen

explanation.surface: A writer is said to resemble a tree, a whimsical comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with trembling leaves, a common deciduous species.

clue.text: Old Japanese fighter creating odd setback in Asia somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are combined in some new order
setback says the word for odd is set backwards

parts.note: rum means odd or strange in British slang

explanation.surface: A warrior of old Japan produces a strange reversal in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM turned back by 'setback' gives MUR; the indicator at the end mixes MUR with ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan.

parts.note: Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man pairs up with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Poor quality Scots potato, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the Scots word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: tattie is the Scots word for potato

explanation.surface: A disappointing spud from Scotland, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby, worn and cheap-looking.

clue.text: Last rites written on wood or bone

indicators.note: written on says the letter sits above the next piece in this down entry
Last picks out only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: last letter of rites
pine is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: The final ceremony for the dead is recorded on a wooden or bone tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is the backbone, the column of vertebrae down the back.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone weeps at a wild black bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' looks like the bird, but here it is the verb for bragging.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag or gloat about one's achievements.

indicators.note: during says the answer sits within the run of letters in the next two words

parts.note: the letters run from inside gala into morning

explanation.surface: A famous battle staged during a festive gala in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was the San Antonio mission besieged in 1836 during the Texas Revolution.

clue.text: Greek character steering limo round cold area of London

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: round says the reshuffled letters go around the next piece
steering suggests the limo is driven around, so its letters are reorganised

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Greek person drives a limousine around a chilly part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steering' rearranges LIMO into MLIO, and 'round' puts it around C to give MLICO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimlico is a residential district of central London, near Victoria.

indicators.note: organise asks for the letters of the preceding words to be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone nervous declines to arrange a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as part-payment for a new one, an exchange in a sale.

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the grasses is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses growing in wetlands

explanation.surface: A botanist examines the plants growing in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject, in British usage, is to study it at university.

indicators.note: in places the numeral within the word for the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people at a dance having a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to celebrate noisily and enjoy oneself at a party.

indicators.note: moved says the letters are shifted into a different order

explanation.surface: Agreement that the cats relocated, to everyone's joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is a state of overwhelming happiness or rapture.

clue.text: Nothing is about in outer limits of Kilmarnock but a booth

indicators.note: in puts the middle group between the two edge letters
outer limits of picks only the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: first and last letters of Kilmarnock

indicators.note: about says the word is goes around the zero

parts.note: taken as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: There is nothing on the edge of a Scottish town except a small stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IS around O to give IOS, and 'in' sets that between K and K. Kilmarnock is a town in Ayrshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk is a small open-fronted hut selling newspapers or snacks, a kind of stall.

indicators.note: in places the word lip within the word for drinks

parts.note: sups means drinks, takes small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Mistakes made by someone bringing their lip to their drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip-ups are careless errors or minor mistakes.

clue.text: Shoot indefinite number out of season

indicators.note: out of says the number is taken from the season's name

parts.note: spring is a season of the year
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Firing an uncertain number of rounds out of hunting season.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or shoot of a plant.

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Carol blended a shade of rosy paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is the pinkish-orange hue of the reef-building sea creatures' skeletons.

indicators.note: foreign suggests the word is made strange, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Welcoming an exotic bird that wades in water.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron that wades in shallow water.

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters stray from their order and settle in a new one

explanation.surface: Couples strolling around a town together.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France, a major European metropolis.

indicators.note: in places the numeral within the reworked letters
accident suggests the word road is wrecked into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with someone involved in a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' rearranges ROAD into RADO, and 'in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio someone is to communicate with them by wireless transmission.

parts.note: on means connected, switched on
in horse racing the going is the state of the turf

explanation.surface: A racing report about how the grass is affected by the latest weather.
explanation.walkthrough: In British racing the 'going' (firm, soft, heavy) describes the state of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Ongoing describes something still in progress, present and continuing now.

indicators.note: almost says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: The boss nearly commits a foolish error.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is an embarrassing social blunder or faux pas.

clue.text: One northern girl in US state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Diana is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A single girl from the north living in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a Midwestern state whose capital is Indianapolis.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stroke of chance good luck
second meaning: a flounder or similar flat sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler gets lucky by landing a flat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a chance success and is also the name of a flounder-like fish.

definitions.note: read as 'capital city is', with the answer as subject

indicators.note: wrong suggests the old capital's name is set out in the incorrect order

explanation.surface: Someone claims Kyoto is Japan's capital and is told they are mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a true correction: Kyoto was the old imperial capital, but today's capital is its letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the present seat of Japan's government, its national capital.

parts.note: le is French for the
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Directions to take someone to a tree from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is a dog's lead, the strap used to walk it.
